palindrome:
Here is an example of a 301-character palindrome:

"A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" (ignoring case and punctuation) written out fully would be:
A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

This sentence is a famous palindrome that includes all the letters of the English alphabet in a specific order. It's often used as an example of a perfect palindrome because it uses every letter exactly once.

Palindrome is a word, phrase, number, or other sequence of characters which reads the same forward and backward, ignoring spaces, punctuation, and capitalization.
